Maya R: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on small-batch seqlen=64 jobs after yesterday's kernel sensor tweak. p99 latency up ~18% on some nodes :frowning:
Leo T: Which nodes? SM versions and model config?
Maya R: Mixed farm: sm_86 and sm_95. The autotuner is switching to a 'wide_matmul_v2' kernel on sm95 for seqlen=64. Previously it picked 'narrow_kv_fast' and we saw far fewer kernel launches and much better KV cache locality.
Sam K: Can you paste the profiler snippet or tracer output? nvprof or our lightweight trace is fine.
Maya R: Sure — quick paste from our trace collector (trimmed):
```
seqlen=64 batch=2 model=30B
previous: narrow_kv_fast  launches=1  total_ms=12.3  avg_ms=12.3  kv_hits=0.71
current: wide_matmul_v2  launches=3  total_ms=17.5  avg_ms=5.8   kv_hits=0.39
kernel_switch_time=2024-11-08T03:04:12Z
```
Maya R: Notice KV hitrate drop and more launches — looks like the chosen kernel forces a different KV layout and evicts hot prefixes.
Leo T: Hmm. Did the device fingerprint change? We recently tweaked the tensor-core hint threshold in the sensor. Maybe it started preferring TC kernels on sm95.
Sam K: Also check driver/properties: sometimes compute capability + driver combo flips our bf16/tc/warp-size heuristics.
Maya R: I ran the quick probe: 
```
$ runtime-probe --device 7 --brief
compute_capability=9.5
tensor_cores=true
bf16_supported=true
fp8_fastpath=false
memory_bus_width=512
```
Maya R: The sensor emitted a soft-confidence bump for TC on sm95 and our autotuner threshold was 0.6 -> it now prefers the TC-optimized path.
Leo T: That matches. We changed the 'prefer_tensorcore' gate from 0.65 to 0.6 in yesterday's change to be more aggressive.
Sam K: Two quick mitigations: 1) Add hysteresis in the kernel sensor (require N consistent samples across batches before switching) 2) Make kernel selection aware of KV cache hitrate — bias toward cached path when kv_hit > X.
Maya R: Agreed. Hysteresis seems safer at first. For heavy KV workloads, prefer cached kernel even if TC_hint is slightly higher.
Leo T: I'd implement both: hysteresis (N=3 by default) + KV bias (bias_coef=0.4). Also emit a metric 'kernel_switch_window' to detect flip-flopping.
Maya R: I'll open a small patch with hysteresis + kv-bias and run a canary on dedicated pool-7. Will attach KV hitrate and kernel_choice metrics.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy started for maya/kernel-sensor-hysteresis at 4301234590 — route: dedicated-gpu-pool-7.
Sam K: Nice. Also add a unit/regression harness for mixed-SM farms with bursty seqlen=64 traffic so this doesn't regress silently.
Leo T: If the canary looks good, let's roll back the aggressive threshold change and add a mapping table keyed by (sm_major, seqlen_range) so we don't rely only on soft thresholds.
Maya R: Will do. Initial KV metrics before patch: cache_hit=0.42, after hysteresis and favoring cached path we expect >0.6 to justify persistent switch.
Maya R: Quick status update — canary started, collecting traces. Early signal: p95 down ~10% and KV hitrate up to 0.66 on the canary hosts. Will keep monitoring for 60m :eyes:
Leo T: Excellent. If stable, promote to non-dedicated pools and then finalize config defaults.
Maya R: Thanks — posting full perf dump and PR link shortly.
